affected_system: heat-health surveillance, prevention, and care coordination
alternatives: advance high-risk work within verified feasible windows for heat-health surveillance and escalation schedule
use rolling risk and capacity updates to reschedule heat-health surveillance and escalation schedule
pair forecast- and syndrome-triggered operations scheduling with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Health records are privacy-preserving, population-defined, timely, and separated from service-request proxies.
Heat exposure, care seeking, reporting, and intervention effects remain distinct constructs.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue the fixed operating calendar for heat-health surveillance and escalation schedule.

constraints.description: The heat-health surveillance and prevention schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: public-health preparedness director and emergency medical services lead
decision_question: When should surveillance refresh, outreach, clinical staffing, and escalation thresholds activate?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The heat-health surveillance and prevention schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for heat-health surveillance and escalation schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.
independence_key.primary_outcome: hours of high-risk conditions without active health response

intended_claim: A versioned schedule design for comparing declared alternatives affecting heat-health surveillance and escalation schedule, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: hours of high-risk conditions without active health response
distributional gap in hours of high-risk conditions without active health response
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call an escalation schedule activated or a health response delivered.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for heat-health surveillance and escalation schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.

title: Schedule heat-health surveillance and response escalation
transportability_risks: Clinical coding, surveillance coverage, acclimatization, housing, and care access vary.
Small-area health estimates may be unstable or disclosure-sensitive.
